description:
The active workspace tag catalog, in deterministic name order. Each entry carries the stable canonical `id` documents store and its current display `name`. Retired entries are absent here but remain visible, marked retired, on documents that still carry them. MCP cannot curate this catalog.

`complete` says whether this is the whole workspace vocabulary. name: create_doc
title: Create a document

title.description: Display title. Identity is the document's UUID, never this. A decision title names the stable topic or question, never the answer; successors keep the title. Example: "Exact behavior of milestone setting `gate`", not "Milestone gate skips milestones with nothing to start". Use one to three short answer blocks with brief reasons; a superseding record carries the new answer. Do not repeat the topic as a "Topic:" line or write a specification: detailed behavior and guidance belong on the related regular page, discussion in the RFC. Answer blocks are distinct from recorded answer: {who, when, where}.

description.description: Agent-facing description used to choose whether to open the document.

tldr.description: One or two sentences of plain English for a person opening the document. At most 300 characters; null clears it.

when.description: When the person gave the answer, preferably an ISO date-time.

where.description: Where the answer was given, such as a conversation or review URL.

answer.description: Record a person's answer, not the agent's own approval. MCP does not verify its provenance.

kind.description: The document's record kind. Omit it for an ordinary working document.

status.description: The recorded lifecycle state. Its kind owns the legal values.

related.description: Live, locally readable regular document UUID this decision relates to. Fixed at creation; omitted successors inherit their predecessor's page. Accepted only with `kind: decision`.

discussion.description: Live, locally readable regular document UUID holding this record's RFC discussion. Accepted only with `kind: decision`; never inherited. Correct or clear with set_metadata only while open; fixed after leaving open. Does not create or tag a document.

supersedes.description: Earlier decision UUID this new decision replaces. Immutable and accepted only with `kind: decision`.

text.description: Block text. A table takes exactly one GFM table with inline Markdown cell formatting; alignment is not stored. A card takes the content between exact :::card and ::: lines: lowercase label, title and footer at most once, a required nonempty title, any number of button lines, then a blank line and optional prose body. Prose header values are one-line inline Markdown, not YAML; quotes stay literal. Each button has one [Text](destination) link: nonempty plain text and an https URL or claude://code/new, claude-cli://open or codex://new, alone or with ?query. At most one style (outline/filled) and color (neutral/blue/green/violet) may follow in either order; defaults are outline neutral. Invalid buttons, other trailing text, unknown, duplicate prose or non-key headers refuse with invalid_card. Prose parts support code, bold, italic, strike, external and document links. Export orders label, title, footer, then buttons in authored order, writes style before color and omits default words. Empty prose keys are omitted, prose header newlines fold to spaces, and prose lines starting ::: are escaped. Figma takes the content between :::figma and :::; required url, optional literal plain one-line title and whole-pixel height 240–960 (default 480), then a blank line and optional caption with the same inline marks. Keys are lowercase, each at most once. Only https figma.com/www.figma.com links to design, file, proto, board, slides or community/file are accepted, with a key/id and optional name; saving keeps those path parts and node-id, starting-point-node-id and version-id on https://www.figma.com, dropping other query fields and fragments. Invalid content refuses with invalid_figma and writes nothing; figma blocks take figma.com links only; use a plain link for other sites. get_doc returns canonical text and read-only figma kind, file, optional fileName and node. Source blocks remain literal text.

language.description: Code language, e.g. "ts". Code blocks only.

inline.description:
Formatted content for a PROSE block (paragraph, heading, list-item, quote), as runs of equally-marked text: `[{text, marks}]`, where marks are `bold`, `italic`, `strike`, `inlineCode`, `link` (an external http(s) URL) and `docLink` (another document's UUID — the inline way to cite one). When present it REPLACES `text`, so the run texts joined together are the block's text. Code, mermaid, terminal and chart hold source text and ignore it; tables, cards and figma also ignore it and read inline Markdown through `text`: exactly one GFM table or the content between :::card/:::figma and :::.

A `docLink` run with an EMPTY `text` is filled in for you with the target's current title, so `{text: "", marks: {docLink: "<uuid>"}}` is how you cite a document without looking its title up first. A target this replica's directory has never heard of fails the call with `doclink_target_not_known_locally` and writes nothing; an archived target is fine.

sidebar.description: Optional sidebar placement. Omitted, the document is created unpinned — alive and reachable, simply not an entry point.

id.description: An EXISTING group's id, as get_sidebar returns it. Never a name: an unknown id fails the call.

position.description: Position in the group, clamped into range. Omitted means last.

Do not repeat the topic as a "Topic:" line or write a specification: detailed behavior and guidance belong on the related regular page, discussion in the RFC. Answer blocks are distinct from recorded answer: {who, when, where}.

description:
Create doc/stub; optional blocks/regular-page TL;DR. Require nonblank title/description. Active tag ids/exact names; unknown/retired refuse. Kind defaults to first status; invalid pairs refuse. Decision title names stable topic, never answer; successors keep it. Example: "Exact behavior of milestone setting `gate`", not "Milestone gate skips milestones with nothing to start". 1–3 short answer blocks with brief reasons; successors give new answer. No "Topic:" line or specification: details/guidance on related page, discussion in RFC. Unsupported/excess blocks/TL;DR refuse. Open/decided; deciding needs valid nonblank blocks, no TL;DR/data; decided successors need recorded human answer. related: live, locally readable regular page; successors inherit unless supplied. supersedes: hydrated decision in live topic. Targets validated pre-write. discussion: live, readable non-decision RFC UUID; reuse/create first; ordinary rfc tag in new workspaces. Never inherited; set_metadata corrects/clears while open, then fixed. RFC/page untouched. Separate from curated links/recorded answer {who, when, where}. Sidebar: get_sidebar group id; invalid = group_not_found, no creation; omit = unpinned. Independent rooms: persistence_failed: uuid, completed/failed, rolledBack: false, duplicate-safe recovery. answerPreview: legacy TL;DR/first paragraph/list; discussion UUID/null, absent if unknown. Page get_doc: related/linked topics.

description:
Read metadata, blocks and threads. Regular pages return related then linked decision topics; decisions return discussion (RFC UUID or null), separate from curated links and recorded answer attribution. Entries cache discussion (absent if unknown) and answerPreview (legacy TL;DR or first paragraph/list, max 300 chars). Missing description/TL;DR is null; data lists collections/counts for get_data. Blocks include rev. Tables return canonical GFM; cards return button: [Text](destination) lines after footer in authored order. Plain labels link to https or exact claude://code/new, claude-cli://open, codex://new, optionally with ?query. Style outline/filled and color neutral/blue/green/violet default to outline neutral; output puts style before color and omits defaults. Figma returns :::figma content without delimiters: normalized url, optional plain title and height, blank line and marked caption. Read-only figma: kind (frame, file, prototype, board, slides or community file), file, optional decoded fileName (dashes as spaces) and optional node (12:345 form). Tables/cards/Figma have formatting-sensitive rev, including every button's text, destination, appearance and order; other rev ignores marks. Prose doc_links has ranges; container links have none. Card thread ranges name their part; Figma ranges name caption with caption-text offsets. No Figma request; eligible guidance counts toward this process's briefing.

description:
Read a document's structured data without changing it, including merged invalidity and diagnostics. Omit collection for an area summary with no schemas or values, or data: null when absent. Name a collection for its raw schema and a detached page in Unicode code-point id order; an unknown collection refuses. after is an exclusive cursor; ids optionally filters it and reports missing_ids. limit: 0 reads only the schema. max_bytes bounds canonical JSON of the page's id/value array, excluding schemas, diagnostics and formatting; a positive-limit page includes its first remaining record even over budget. It does not bound the whole response or token count. Follow next_after until complete; schema-only reads do not advance, and pages are not snapshots.

description:
Apply one validated batch through applyDocData, naming each touched collection once. Within each collection, set `schema`, optionally `replaceRecords`, then `deleteRecords`, then `upsert` whole `{id, value}` records. `deleteCollection: true` excludes other changes. Schema and value JSON reach validation unaltered; unsupported schemas and invalid retained records refuse before mutation. The batch is one local transaction; identical refreshes return `changed: false` without an update. The result summarizes touched collection names, counts and deletion with durability, without values.

Refresh producer-owned collections by upsert or full-set replacement. Keep human dispositions in a separate collection keyed by producer record ids. Split changes above the 1 MiB schema/value budget across calls; they are not atomic together and supply no CAS or distributed lock. Read with get_data; get_doc summarizes collections. Decisions refuse data with decision_data_unsupported; decided records keep decision_read_only, and legacy data stays readable. Decisions use one to three short answer blocks with a brief reason, guidance on the related regular page and discussion in an RFC. Their directory answerPreview uses legacy TL;DR or the first paragraph/list; get_doc page decisions are marked related or linked. Recorded attribution {who, when, where} is separate from the answer's content blocks.

description:
List synced directory stubs without opening document rooms. Unfiltered listing omits decisions; kind, status, tag or has_open_threads predicates include matching decisions. Topic rows present the record in force, else pending, else first, plus pending/conflicting records. Predicates may match different live records; resolution uses the whole graph. include_superseded applies predicates per record. include_deleted admits archived entries, never permanently deleted UUIDs, and is not a predicate. Filters combine; unknown tags refuse. has_open_threads accepts only true: known openThreadCount >= 1; false refuses. Every entry, including inForce, pending and conflicts, caches its document's openThreadCount: threads whose resolved is not true, including deleted anchors; absent means unknown. A matching topic's representative may have zero or unknown count. Use include_superseded: true with has_open_threads to find each matching document, then get_doc for threads and annotate to reply or resolve. Rows carry cached description, tags, lifecycle/authority metadata, sidebar-derived pinned and optional approximate timestamps. Decision answerPreview is legacy TL;DR or first paragraph/list, null for none; discussion is its explicit RFC UUID, null for none, distinct from curated links and recorded answer. Both are absent when unknown. get_doc marks related or linked topics.

description:

English word forms match; case and accents fold, underscore groups match adjacent words and a trailing * matches prefixes. Punctuation or emoji alone matches nothing. description:
Splice block text, preserving edits elsewhere. Assert old_text and preferably rev from get_doc; stale_block or old_text_mismatch returns currentText/currentRev. Assertions are replica-local. Edit prose strictly inside unmarked text; replace marked spans with delete_block/insert_block and verify export_markdown. Tables require GFM old/new text and table_mapping for structural/multi-cell edits. Cards take :::card content: inline-Markdown prose, repeated button: [Text](destination) lines after footer in authored order. New buttons need nonempty plain labels linking to https or exact claude://code/new, claude-cli://open, codex://new, optionally with ?query. Style outline/filled and color neutral/blue/green/violet default to outline neutral; output writes style before color and omits defaults. invalid_card refuses bad input; unchanged parts, buttons and anchors survive. Rev includes each button's text, destination, appearance and order. Figma takes :::figma content: url, optional plain title and height 240–960, blank line and marked caption. Accepted Figma view URLs retain only the path and node-id, starting-point-node-id, version-id on www.figma.com. invalid_figma refuses without writing. Changed headers update their fields; unchanged caption marks/anchors survive. Figma rev includes caption formatting. Card/Figma conversions and table_mapping are refused; new document targets must be known locally.

uuid.description: Document UUID.

after_block_id.description: Insert after this block. Omit or null to insert first.

text.description: Block text. A table takes exactly one GFM table with inline Markdown cell formatting; alignment is not stored. A card takes the content between exact :::card and ::: lines: lowercase label, title and footer at most once, a required nonempty title, any number of button lines, then a blank line and optional prose body. Prose header values are one-line inline Markdown, not YAML; quotes stay literal. Each button has one [Text](destination) link: nonempty plain text and an https URL or claude://code/new, claude-cli://open or codex://new, alone or with ?query. At most one style (outline/filled) and color (neutral/blue/green/violet) may follow in either order; defaults are outline neutral. Invalid buttons, other trailing text, unknown, duplicate prose or non-key headers refuse with invalid_card. Prose parts support code, bold, italic, strike, external and document links. Export orders label, title, footer, then buttons in authored order, writes style before color and omits default words. Empty prose keys are omitted, prose header newlines fold to spaces, and prose lines starting ::: are escaped. Figma takes the content between :::figma and :::; required url, optional literal plain one-line title and whole-pixel height 240–960 (default 480), then a blank line and optional caption with the same inline marks. Keys are lowercase, each at most once. Only https figma.com/www.figma.com links to design, file, proto, board, slides or community/file are accepted, with a key/id and optional name; saving keeps those path parts and node-id, starting-point-node-id and version-id on https://www.figma.com, dropping other query fields and fragments. Invalid content refuses with invalid_figma and writes nothing; figma blocks take figma.com links only; use a plain link for other sites. get_doc returns canonical text and read-only figma kind, file, optional fileName and node. Source blocks remain literal text.

language.description: Code language, e.g. "ts". Code blocks only.

inline.description:
Formatted content for a PROSE block (paragraph, heading, list-item, quote), as runs of equally-marked text: `[{text, marks}]`, where marks are `bold`, `italic`, `strike`, `inlineCode`, `link` (an external http(s) URL) and `docLink` (another document's UUID — the inline way to cite one). When present it REPLACES `text`, so the run texts joined together are the block's text. Code, mermaid, terminal and chart hold source text and ignore it; tables, cards and figma also ignore it and read inline Markdown through `text`: exactly one GFM table or the content between :::card/:::figma and :::.

A `docLink` run with an EMPTY `text` is filled in for you with the target's current title, so `{text: "", marks: {docLink: "<uuid>"}}` is how you cite a document without looking its title up first. A target this replica's directory has never heard of fails the call with `doclink_target_not_known_locally` and writes nothing; an archived target is fine.

description:
Set title, description, tldr, tags, curated links or decision discussion together; name at least one. Omitted fields stay unchanged. Refusals write nothing; field failures name field. Returns metadata/durability, no TL;DR hint/mark. Title/description cannot be empty/cleared. tldr: null clears while preserving the mark; marked pages refuse a summary with tldr_opted_out unless tldr_opt_in: true accompanies non-null tldr. MCP cannot mark pages. Tags/links replace sets; [] clears. Use list_tags active ids/exact names; assigned retired/unresolved ids may remain. New links must be directory-known; archived/unchanged targets accepted. Only open decisions accept discussion: a live, locally readable non-decision RFC UUID or null. Reuse/create RFC first; no document creation, RFC/page edits or tags, or approvalFingerprint/approvalChanged changes. Discussion is separate from curated links/recorded answer, fixed after settling. Decisions refuse non-null tldr with decision_tldr_unsupported; null clears legacy TL;DR. Decided records refuse title/tldr/discussion; description/tags/links writable. Decision answers use one to three short answer blocks and a brief reason; guidance on related page, discussion in RFC. Stub answerPreview uses legacy TL;DR/first paragraph/list; get_doc marks related or linked topics. Recorded answer {who, when, where} is attribution. Archived documents refuse metadata; lifecycle uses set_status.

description:
Mark selected prose text as a document reference without changing its characters or rev. start/end are character offsets measured against the required rev; stale_block returns currentText/currentRev for remeasurement. Indices clamp to text and swap if reversed; empty ranges refuse. Existing document references are retargeted; external links, source blocks, tables, cards and Figma blocks refuse. Write card and Figma caption links as inline Markdown in their container text. doc_id must be known to this replica's directory or doclink_target_not_known_locally refuses before writing; archived targets are accepted. The answer includes the target title, but the label stays the selected text and does not follow renames. Backlinks update without changing curated meta.links.

description:
Render a Markdown projection: code, mermaid, terminal and chart keep source fences; tables write padded GFM with inline cell marks. Cards export separate :::card containers with inline-Markdown prose and button: [Text](destination) lines after footer in authored order. Each exported button's plain label links to https or exact claude://code/new, claude-cli://open, codex://new, optionally with ?query. Style outline/filled and color neutral/blue/green/violet default to outline neutral; export writes style before color and omits defaults. Import restores buttons and appearances. Figma exports separate :::figma containers: url, optional literal title and height, blank line and marked caption. Normalized HTTPS www.figma.com links retain design/file/proto/board/slides/community/file path, key/id, optional name and node-id, starting-point-node-id, version-id; other query values and fragments were dropped at save. Absent keys are omitted; header newlines fold to spaces and prose lines starting ::: are escaped. Import restores caption marks and adjacent containers; invalid/unclosed containers remain literal paragraphs. MCP refuses bad Figma content with invalid_figma; get_doc derives kind/file/fileName/node. Markdown help owns height 240–960 and accepted links. Export contacts no Figma service. Chart/data records are omitted with a notice; Markdown is never storage and MCP has no import tool.

description:
Inspect local replica state, pending rooms and hub connection/acknowledgements. hub.status distinguishes disabled, retryable hub-down, auth-failed requiring action, and update-required protocol mismatch. hub.recoveryClass, authRecovery and reason explain recovery; protocolVersion and hubProtocolVersion identify the incompatible side. Tools still work locally. unsyncedChanges counts durable pending rooms; inFlightUpdates counts provider sync messages on the current connection, resetting on reconnect. lastSync is this machine's stored UTC time when its full replica caught up, or null; it never moves backwards across processes. persistence diagnoses a failed log append and remains readable when ordinary replica tools are quarantined until restart. See this tool's help for counter units and lastSync conditions.

description:
Pin a document into a group, creating the group when no group carries that name. `index` places it; omit it to append.

One pin per document across the whole sidebar, so this is also how a pinned document is moved or reordered: pinning one that is already pinned moves it to `index` in the named group — carrying the pin as it stands rather than re-pinning it, so a concurrent unpin still wins — and `index` then counts positions in the target group after the document has been taken out of it.

description:
Remove a document from the sidebar, wherever it sits. The document itself is untouched: unpinning is a navigation act. archive_doc hides a document; delete_doc permanently deletes an archived regular document.

An unpin beats a move made concurrently on another replica, so a document does not reappear because somebody was dragging it at the time. It takes no group: one pin per document means there is only ever one place to remove it from. `unpinned` is false when the document was not pinned to begin with.

description:
Manage the groups themselves. `delete` removes the group and its pins — the documents are untouched, because the group only ever held their uuids, and they stay reachable through list_docs and search.

`action` picks one of three shapes and each takes only its own field: `rename` needs `name` and refuses `index`, `move` takes `index` (omitted: last) and refuses `name`, `delete` takes neither. A field belonging to another action is refused at the input boundary before the sidebar is touched, rather than ignored — so a call that says two things is a failure you can see, not a silent half-success.

There is no create action: pin_doc creates a group by naming one that does not exist, which is how a group comes into being with something in it rather than empty.
